findings.reason: the section's stated keying rule is unimplementable for the dialect it is about, so the node would invent a source for the prompt instruction and could ship an instruction naming an absent tool.
findings.text: the deliverable states both changes are "keyed on the run's recorded anchored_edit fact, as §5 does for codex", but §4 (line 79) defines that record as what the launch actually did — false with reason unfenced, operator-settings or resumed even when the flight key is true — and §5 records that dispatch composes the prompt before the launch plan exists (dispatch.py:2942 against the record at dispatch_launch.py:3539); a node following this sentence must either key the prompt on the flight key, which tells an unfenced or operator-settings Claude run to use a tool it does not have, or read a record that does not exist yet, whereas §5's "key and launch cannot disagree" argument is explicitly true only for codex

findings.reason: as written the node's own gate is unreachable unless it picks one particular route, which forces the measurement the Why says is still open rather than letting the node establish it.
findings.text: the done-when requires "a test shows the launch environment and prompt for a Claude-dialect anchored run carry the fix and the instruction", and its negative control removes "the startup allowance, the faster start or the prompt route, whichever it is", but two of those three routes leave the launch environment identical to the baseline: making the server start faster is a change in the server process, and the prompt route is a change in the composed prompt, so neither can make a launch-environment assertion pass, nor make it fail when removed

findings.reason: without the before record having to fail, the section's experimental half cannot demonstrate the mechanism it exists to establish, and the fix can ship unverified.
findings.text: the pre-fix headless session is recorded but never required to fail the acceptance criterion, which is stated only for the fixed session ("the fixed session counts as offering the tools when the anchored server's session-start status is connected and either its tools are in the session-start tool list or a ToolSearch for them in that session returns them"), so a node can record two sessions that both satisfy it and still close; under the deferral mechanism the server is connected in both, so the criterion alone cannot show the fix changed anything

findings.reason: the acceptance test admits the exact failure mode §10 exists to catch, and §8's edit-failure metric would inherit the same blind spot.
findings.text: the closing run's criterion is "its stream shows edit_anchored calls with no file edits made through Bash", but §4 keeps Write in the arm ("Write stays, because creating a file has no anchor to address") and Write rewrites an existing file, so a run that performs every edit by rewriting files through Write and makes one edit_anchored call satisfies the criterion while measuring the same 'no anchored edits' outcome the section was written to repair

findings.reason: both upstreams are already done, so declaring the edge changes no dispatch order today; it would only matter if the plan were re-ordered or a section were reopened.
findings.text: the plan-section-depends-on map names s4, s5, s7 and s8 but gives s10 no entry, although s10's server-registration behaviour is §4's seeder and its prompt instruction is the compose_prompt seam §5 added

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the cited run directory exists, its worker.json records anchored_edit: true, its stream holds 93 Bash, 4 Write, 1 Edit and 0 anchored calls over 42 offered tools with reckon-anchored-edit pending and total_deferred_tools: 39, and the clive-anchored backend is declared in flight.yaml.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the launch-environment and prompt test, and the negative control that must make it fail, are satisfiable only when the node picks the startup-allowance route, though the deliverable permits three routes.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both session records are kept as gate logs in the run's durable log directory and the transcript beside them, not in a scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §10 adds no symbol, filename or comment and carries no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the deliverable says both changes are "keyed on the run's recorded anchored_edit fact, as §5 does for codex", but §4 defines that recorded fact as what the launch actually did and it is written after the prompt is composed, so for the Claude dialect the prompt cannot be keyed on it and nothing states what the prompt should be keyed on instead.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §10 names one endpoint, a Claude-dialect anchored run being offered the tool and told to use it, and both deliverable changes serve that one measure.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §10 consumes §4's per-run server registration and §5's compose_prompt instruction yet declares no plan-section-depends-on entry, while the meta block names dependencies for s4, s5, s7 and s8 only.
